definitions.explanation: A Japanese banknote with a face value of 5,000 yen. One of the standard denominations of Japanese paper currency.

examples.japanese: {五千円札|ごせんえんさつ}で{払|はら}ってもいいですか。
examples.english: Can I pay with a five-thousand-yen bill?

examples.japanese: {財布|さいふ}に{五千円札|ごせんえんさつ}が{一枚|いちまい}{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: There is one five-thousand-yen bill in my wallet.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{五千円札|ごせんえんさつ}のデザインには{津田梅子|つだうめこ}の{肖像|しょうぞう}が{使|つか}われている。
examples.english: The new five-thousand-yen bill features a portrait of Tsuda Umeko.

notes:
The {五千円札|ごせんえんさつ} is one of four denominations of Japanese banknotes. As of 2024, the bill features {津田梅子|つだうめこ}, a pioneer in women's education in Japan. The previous design (2004-2024) featured {樋口一葉|ひぐちいちよう}, a Meiji-era novelist.

JAPANESE BANKNOTE DENOMINATIONS:
- {千円札|せんえんさつ}: 1,000 yen bill
- {五千円札|ごせんえんさつ}: 5,000 yen bill
- {一万円札|いちまんえんさつ}: 10,000 yen bill

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {五千円札|ごせんえんさつ}で{払|はら}う: to pay with a 5,000-yen bill
- {五千円札|ごせんえんさつ}を{崩|くず}す: to break a 5,000-yen bill (into smaller bills/coins)
- {五千円札|ごせんえんさつ}に{両替|りょうがえ}する: to exchange for a 5,000-yen bill

CULTURAL NOTE:
In daily life, the {五千円札|ごせんえんさつ} is commonly used for mid-range purchases. When giving money as a gift (ご{祝儀|しゅうぎ}), odd numbers of bills are preferred, making this denomination useful.
